rationale:
Issue 1709 ('named tuple in closure argument destructuring breaks after formatting') reports that preferForLoop rewrote `dict.forEach { (header: (key: String, value: String)) in ... }` into `for (header, value) in dict`, producing code that no longer compiles. PR 1712 body states 'This PR fixes #1709' and reproduces the same input/output pair, and traceability resolves fix_commit_to_merged_pr_to_issue for verified issue 1709. The root cause is visible in the single production hunk: the buggy code split the entire argument-list token range on `.delimiter(",")`, so the comma nested inside the tuple type was treated as an argument separator and yielded two argument names for one argument; the fix walks top-level identifier labels, appending only labels that follow a top-level comma. The minimized patch retains 1 of 1 hunk in Sources/ParsingHelpers.swift with post-minimization validation PASS; it is behavior-only, adds no options, rule, or public API, and the single added comment line is explanatory text inside the replacement logic rather than a documentation-only change. The trigger is the unchanged upstream test testForEachOverDictionary from the same fixing commit, using the pre-existing testFormatting(for:output:rule:) helper and pre-existing FormatRules.preferForLoop, so no fix-only API is referenced; strict evidence confirms build.both_versions PASS, trigger.buggy_differential reproducing exactly ['Tests/RulesTests+Syntax.swift::testForEachOverDictionary'], trigger.deterministic over 3 repetitions, trigger.fixed_clean, and full_suite.fixed_all_green, in both strict_original and strict_post_minimization with no failed checks. The expected `for header in dict` output matches one of the acceptable outcomes described in the issue (single-argument semantics preserved) rather than new behavior introduced by the fix. active_same_project_root_causes is empty and nicklockwood/swiftformat#1709 is the sole allowed verified key, so no duplicate exists.

Issue 1709 reports that `dict.forEach { (header: (key: String, value: String)) in ... }` was rewritten by preferForLoop into `for (header, value) in dict`, breaking compilation. The single production hunk in Sources/ParsingHelpers.swift replaces the naive `split(separator: .delimiter(","))` over the whole argument-list token range (which also split on commas nested inside the tuple type, yielding two argument names for one argument) with a scan that only collects top-level argument labels. That is exactly the parse error described in the issue and in PR 1712 ('This PR fixes #1709'), which is linked to the fix commit via fix_commit_to_merged_pr_to_issue. The minimized patch is one behavioral hunk with no refactor, formatting, docs, config, or test content; the only added comment describes the new loop. The trigger is the unchanged upstream test testForEachOverDictionary from the same fixing commit, using the pre-existing testFormatting(for:output:rule:) helper and pre-existing FormatRules.preferForLoop, and it asserts the exact reproducer from the issue body, so it builds and runs on both revisions with no fix-only API. Strict evidence shows build.both_versions PASS, trigger.buggy_differential reproducing Tests/RulesTests+Syntax.swift::testForEachOverDictionary, trigger.fixed_clean PASS, deterministic across 3 repetitions and a 32-run matrix, and full_suite.fixed_all_green PASS both originally and post-minimization. No active same-project root causes are registered, so this is not a duplicate. The assertion expecting `for header in dict` (rather than the issue author's alternative suggestion of `for (key, value) in dict`) is a correct resolution of the same mis-parse, not a feature extension.
